To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
p15(INKB4B) is a CDKI that is able to block cell cycle progression at G2/M in cells lacking wild type Rb.

p15(INKB) can inhibit growth of cells lacking Rb, as well as cells with wild type pRb expression, that the Rb-independent effect requires ankyrin structures and that this effect is associated with a decrease in the number of cells in G2M phases of the cell.
p15(INK 4B) is able to inhibit cell cycle progression in cells with wild-type Rb as well in those without Rb.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of p15( INK4B) in the regulation of the cell cycle, and the mechanism by which this occurs.
the mechanism of growth arrest caused by overexpression and the role of p15(ING4B) and other CDK inhibitors.
understanding the mechanisms by which CDKIs regulate cell growth and the role of CDKIs in the pathogenesis of human cancers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the p15(INK)4B protein is capable of inhibiting the cell cycle in the G2/M phases and is not dependent on the Rb protein for this function.
the Rb protein is not the sole target of the INK4 family CDKI.
the inhibition of cell growth is Rb independent and mediated by the ankyrin structures of p15(ink4b) and that this inhibition is caused by a block of progression from G1 into S phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Rb independent inhibition by p15(INk4B) is mediated by an ankyrin dependent pathway.
Rb independent cell growth inhibition by p15(ING4B) requires the N-terminal ankyrin structures.
p15(INK) can inhibit cell growth in a Rb independent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the p15(INKB4B) protein has a role in cell cycle progression independent of Rb.
the Rb dependent pathway is only one of several pathways for growth control.
p15(INKA4B) is an effective inhibitor of cell proliferation in cells with wild-type and mutant Rb.
